title: DevHarness Implementation Output
description: Producer output contract for a DevHarness implementation worker after applying its assigned slice.

outcome.description: Producer must emit the single enum value that reflects the completed stage state; use blocked only when blocker explains a concrete external or contract-level recoverable pause.
outcome.x-usage: Treat this as the authoritative workflow state for this output. Do not infer success from other populated fields when this says blocked or needs revision. Verification failures caused by the worker's own in-scope changes are implementation work to fix and rerun, not blockers by themselves.

summary.description: Producer must summarize the completed implementation slice in concise human-readable form without embedding the handoff artifact body.
summary.x-usage: Use this as orientation metadata only. The implementation-handoff artifact is the source of truth for review handoff detail.

changed_files.description: Producer must list repository-relative files changed by this implementation worker.
changed_files.x-usage: Use this for focused file inspection and final reporting. Do not assume unchanged files were inspected or safe.

command.description: Producer must record the command or manual check name exactly enough to reproduce or understand it.
command.x-usage: Use this to reproduce or audit the check. Do not treat it as proof of success without the paired result.

result.description: Producer must record the observed result, including failures, skips, or blockers.
result.x-usage: Treat this as the observed check result, including failures or skips. Do not mark the check as passing unless this says it passed.

verification.description: Producer must list verification commands or checks run for this slice and their results, including any failures and how they were fixed, skipped, or classified.
verification.x-usage: Compare these checks against the required verification. Treat missing, skipped, or failed checks as unresolved until explained or fixed. Self-caused in-scope failures should be fixed and rerun unless doing so requires an external blocker.

artifacts.description: Producer must emit artifact metadata for the required immutable implementation-handoff artifact when outcome is implemented.
artifacts.x-usage: Emit only artifact metadata here; the full implementation handoff body lives in the referenced artifact file.

summary.description: Producer must summarize the relevant decision or handoff in concise human-readable form without adding new scope.
summary.x-usage: Use this as concise human-readable context only. Do not route, approve, or expand scope from this text.

source_step_id.description: Producer must name the workflow step id that found or owns this blocker or finding.
source_step_id.x-usage: Use this to identify the step that found or owns the blocker/finding. Do not treat it as a retry target by itself.

needed.description: Producer must state the exact missing decision, permission, input, or evidence required to proceed.
needed.x-usage: Surface this exact missing input, permission, evidence, or decision before proceeding. Do not substitute assumptions for it.

evidence.description: Producer should list concrete evidence references supporting this handoff, verdict, finding, or blocker.
evidence.x-usage: Use these references to inspect or challenge the claim. Do not assume unreferenced surfaces were checked.

risk.description: Producer should describe the residual risk if this blocker or finding is ignored.
risk.x-usage: Use this to understand why ignoring the item is unsafe. Treat it as risk context unless paired with a blocked outcome.

blocker.description: Producer must populate this when outcome is blocked, naming the recoverable pause reason, owning step, and specific missing input, permission, approved-contract change, redesign/plan decision, or unsafe repo/environment state.
blocker.x-usage: Treat this as a recoverable pause. Surface the missing input or decision, then continue this same workflow step after it is resolved. Do not use blocker for red tests caused by the worker's own in-scope changes unless fixing them requires an external or contract-level recoverable pause.
